Question: A sequence \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots\) of non-negative integers is defined by the rule \(a_{n+2} = |a_{n+1} - a_n|\) for \(n \ge 1.\) If \(a_1 = 999,\) \(a_2 \lt 999,\) and \(a_{2006} = 1,\) how many different values of \(a_2\) are possible?
